issue.title: test_reservation_reads_skip_the_stale_proof_memo flakes under the full parallel lane, passes serially: new sase-tt node with no flake-baseline entry
issue.description: tests/test_agent_name_registry_rebuild.py::test_reservation_reads_skip_the_stale_proof_memo fails twice under the full parallel lane and passes serially in isolation. The node was added two days ago by commit 5a1b88683 (the sase-tt landing) to pin the display-vs-reservation memo split, has no entry in tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt, and both of its failures were recorded after that commit landed -- so it is a live flake, not stale pre-fix evidence. It is one of the 7 nodes currently over the flake baseline, and the only one of the 7 with no bead, so it blocks check-full's last gate for every landing agent.

task_type_fields.evidence:
Found by the sase-tj.10 land agent while running the `flake baseline` gate that `just check-full` never reached (check-full aborted one gate earlier, at `test cost` / sase-j0). Not caused by epic sase-tj.10, whose diff is the Artifacts Agent pane's navigation, `sase agent search` flags, and PNG goldens -- it touches no agent-name registry, reservation, or memo code.

OBSERVATIONS
- Fails: two independent full-lane records in the selection-health store, both on tree 9b7990efb, recorded 2026-08-26T02:05:53Z (20260826T015920Z-9b7990efbe31-709913-full-run.json) and 2026-08-26T05:36:00Z (20260826T052125Z-9b7990efbe31-315157-full-run.json), one failure each. Both records carry tree_dirty=True, and neither qualifies for the gate's dirty-tree source-audit exclusion, so both count as live flake evidence.
- Passes: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_agent_name_registry_rebuild.py::test_reservation_reads_skip_the_stale_proof_memo -q -p no:randomly` on 2026-08-26 in workspace sase_15 at e8de34fe0 -- 1 passed in 3.17s, 1.51s of which is setup.
- So: intermittent under the full parallel lane, green serially in isolation. Fail rate is 2 of the 2 full-lane records that name the node; every other recent full-run record in the store omits it.

WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY COVERED
This node is new. It arrived with commit 5a1b88683 ("fix(agent-names): pay the full staleness proof on reservation reads", the sase-tt landing), which added it to "pin the display/reservation split with a new test". That same commit retired sase-tt's own pre-fix flake evidence, and its sibling `tests/test_agent_name_registry_rebuild.py::test_stale_proof_memo_invalidated_by_mutation` already carries `# fixed-at: 2026-08-25T23:47:42Z` at tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt:266. This node has no baseline entry, and both of its failures were recorded AFTER that fixed-at timestamp, so it is not stale pre-fix evidence being re-counted -- it is a live flake in a test added two days ago. Epic sase-tt is closed, so there is no active epic to attach it to.

WHY IT MATTERS
The flake baseline gate refuses additions without a filed bead ("Additions require a filed bead; fix or file the node before landing"), so this node blocks `just check-full`'s last gate for every landing agent until it is filed or fixed. It is currently one of 7 nodes over the baseline; the other 6 are already filed (sase-ty, sase-r2, sase-tz, sase-u0, sase-u1, and the help-guide node tracked on epic sase-th).

LIKELY ROOT CAUSE TO CHECK FIRST
The test asserts reservation reads bypass the 2s stale-proof registry memo. `_load_registry_for_reservations()` runs with trust_stale_proof_memo=False while display reads keep the memo, so the assertion very likely depends on real wall-clock timing against that 2s memo window -- exactly the shape that loses under parallel-lane CPU starvation while passing serially. Check whether the memo's freshness window is compared against a monotonic clock the test can pin, rather than a real 2s sleep or deadline.
